newsitem.title: USA: Atlantic Coast jet order to boost capacity.
newsitem.headline: Atlantic Coast jet order to boost capacity.

text.p: Atlantic Coast Airlines Inc's 12-jet order from Bombardier Inc will significantly boost the airline's capacity and expand its market focus, Atlantic Coast Chief Executive Kerry Skeen said.
The regional airline said it expects the jet order to increase capacity about 80 percent by September 1998 from the year-end 1996 level.
Atlantic Coast Tuesday ordered 12 Canadair regional jets from Bombardier's regional aircraft division and has options to acquire an additional 36 jets.
The 12-jet order has a retail value of about $240 million. The value of the order would increase to about $960 million if all the options were exercised, Bombardier executives said.
The airline said it does not expect to take any one-time charges for the aircraft acquisition.

Deliveries of the Canadair regional jet series 200 ER 50-seat aircraft are scheduled to begin as early as July with revenue passenger service beginning in September, the airline said. The airline said will take delivery of four aircraft in 1997 and the remaining eight jets in 1998.
The Canadair jet is a 50-seat passenger twin-engine aircraft designed for medium-range and small markets.
The 50-seat jet marks an increase over Atlantic Coast's existing fleet of 29-passenger and 19-passenger Aerospace Jetstream aircraft.
Atlantic Coast currently operates 28 Jetstream 41s, 29 Jetstream 32s and has 12 Jetstream 41s on order, which will be delivered between 1997 and 1999.
Atlantic Coast said it plans to use the jets to capitalize on its position at Washington Dulles International Airport while expanding to other potential routes.
The airline said it expects to add service to new cities along the Eastern Seaboard. The airline currently serves 38 cities in 17 states.
"Our niche remains up and down the Atlantic coast market," Skeen said.
Atlantic Coast operates at Washington Dulles as United Express under a marketing partnership with UAL Corp's United Airlines.
